Receiving a DuckDB result without rounding

Source: vignettes/articles/duckdb.Rmd
duckdb.Rmd

DuckDB stores BIGINT as a 64-bit integer and DECIMAL(38, 0) as a 128-bit one. R’s numbers are doubles, which hold every integer up to 2^53 and only some beyond it. A query that returns an identifier, an amount in cents or a nanosecond timestamp past that point comes back changed, and nothing says so.

This article shows the change happening, then the same result received through zuarrow, which either returns every value exactly or stops and says which column could not be.

library(zuarrow)
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())

The silent change

The query returns two keys. The first is 2^53 + 1, the smallest integer a double cannot hold.

sql <- "SELECT * FROM (VALUES (9007199254740993::BIGINT, 'a'),
                              (1::BIGINT, 'b')) AS t(key, label)"

DBI returns it as a double, rounded to its neighbour.

res <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, sql)
format(res$key, scientific = FALSE)
#> [1] "9007199254740992" "               1"

A join against the exact key would now miss this row.

Exact or error

DuckDB can hand over the same result as an Arrow stream, which zuarrow converts directly.

fetch_arrow <- function(con, sql) {
  res <- DBI::dbSendQuery(con, sql, arrow = TRUE)
  on.exit(DBI::dbClearResult(res))
  reader <- duckdb::duckdb_fetch_record_batch(res)
  stream <- nanoarrow::as_nanoarrow_array_stream(reader)
  arrow_to_r(stream, lossy = "character")
}

By default the conversion refuses, and the error names the column, the row and the ways to receive it exactly.

res <- DBI::dbSendQuery(con, sql, arrow = TRUE)
stream <- nanoarrow::as_nanoarrow_array_stream(
  duckdb::duckdb_fetch_record_batch(res)
)
arrow_to_r(stream)
#> Error in `arrow_to_r()`:
#> ! Column `key` (Arrow format `l`) cannot be converted to R exactly: row 1 holds 9007199254740993. Load zuint to read it exactly, or use `lossy = "character"` for its exact text, or `lossy = "allow"` to accept the loss.
DBI::dbClearResult(res)

With lossy = "character" the key arrives as its exact text, and arrow_array() turns that text back into the same int64.

out <- fetch_arrow(con, sql)
out$key
#> [1] "9007199254740993" "1"               
#> attr(,"arrow_type")
#> [1] "l"
arrow_array(out$key)
#> <zuarrow_array int64[2]>

A package that registers an exact class for int64, such as zuint, makes the default conversion exact, with no argument at all.

Columns that fit

Only columns whose values cannot be held exactly are refused. Keys within 2^53 arrive as ordinary doubles under the default.

small <- "SELECT 42::BIGINT AS key, DATE '2026-10-21' AS day"
res <- DBI::dbSendQuery(con, small, arrow = TRUE)
stream <- nanoarrow::as_nanoarrow_array_stream(
  duckdb::duckdb_fetch_record_batch(res)
)
str(arrow_to_r(stream))
#> 'data.frame':    1 obs. of  2 variables:
#>  $ key: num 42
#>  $ day: Date, format: "2026-10-21"
DBI::dbClearResult(res)
